findings.description: The trigger is a measured delay between release and start. If the task never starts, that delay has no completed start event, so the statement does not clearly require late-start detection while the task is still waiting. CON-SUP-103 defines a late start relative to the configured limit.
findings.requested_change: Clarify whether and when a late-start fault is detected if the task has not started after its limit expires, resolving the behavior with the product owner if necessary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 says an overrun is detected when the execution limit expires. The requirement permits detection only when measured execution time is greater than the limit, and its rationale explicitly delays detection until the first measurement step after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the expiry-time detection rule and equality boundary with the product owner, record any needed open point, and align the requirement with that decision.

findings.description: The statement requires both detection of configuration fault code 9 and latching the safe state. Detection can succeed while the latch fails, so the two behaviors are independently judgeable.
findings.requested_change: Separate configuration-fault detection and safe-state latching into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: This item requires a window-watchdog refresh at the end of every cycle in which no fault is detected. SYS-SUP-013 prohibits every watchdog service action while the safe state is latched and after a fault is detected until reset, including cycles with no new detection.
findings.requested_change: Make the refresh condition explicitly consistent with the persistent fault and latched-state withholding obligations in SYS-SUP-013.
